findings.title: Public group members page lists only the first 50 members, and nothing on the page pages through the rest
findings.description: `members` now defaults `limit` to 50 for every group (line 22). Before this diff, non-automatic groups returned every member, and automatic groups were capped at 200. The public template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6` renders `{{#each m in members}}` with no paging controls. The `group-members` route (`routes/group-members.js.es6:8-12`) calls `findMembers()` once and has no paging action. The group header still shows the full count (`discourse/templates/group.hbs:11`, `counts.members`), so a group of 120 members says 120 but lists 50 with no way to see the rest.

findings.title: totalPages is one page too high when the member count is an exact multiple of the page size, so Next loads an empty page
findings.description: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 pages for exactly 50 members at limit 50, when 1 is correct. `showingLast` (line 17) is therefore false on the real last page, so `next` (lines 29-38) requests offset 50. The server returns an empty `members` list, and the page shows "2/2" with no rows. `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` fixes it.

findings.title: Pressing Enter in the group form clicks the first submit button, which is "Add members", instead of saving
findings.description: The template is wrapped in `<form>` (line 1), but none of its buttons set `type`, so they default to `submit`. Implicit submission clicks the first submit button in tree order. For an existing non-automatic group that is the "Add" button at line 29, which comes before Save (line 47). Pressing Enter in the name input (line 8) therefore runs `addMembers`. If the user-selector has typed usernames, they are added and the group is not saved. Setting `type="button"` on the non-submit buttons, or removing the `<form>`, fixes it.

findings.title: The remove link appears for members of automatic groups, but the server always rejects those removals
findings.description: `{{#unless automatic}}` is resolved against the item context, which is the member `User`, not the group. The group's flag is only visible from the controller, as `group.hbs:25` uses it correctly. So the × renders for every member, including automatic groups. Clicking it sends DELETE, which `remove_member` rejects with 422 (`app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:88`). `removeMember` (`models/group.js:40-49`) has no rejection handler, so the admin sees nothing happen. Referencing `controller.automatic` from the item template should fix it.

findings.title: Adding a username that is already a member raises a unique-constraint error (500) and leaves the batch partly applied
findings.description: `add_members` calls `group.add(user)` for each username (line 73), and `Group#add` is a bare `self.users.push(user)` (`app/models/group.rb:272-274`). `group_users` has a unique index on `(group_id, user_id)` (`db/migrate/20130416004933_group_users.rb:9`), and `GroupUser` has no validation (`app/models/group_user.rb`). Re-adding an existing member therefore raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, which is not rescued. There is no transaction, so users earlier in the list stay added. The UI lets the admin type existing members (`admin-group.js.es6:61-65`), and `Discourse.Group#addMembers` (`models/group.js:51-60`) has no failure handler, so the admin gets no message and the list does not refresh.

findings.title: Removing a member through `group.users.delete` skips the counter-cache callback, so the stored user_count stays too high
findings.description: On a `has_many :through`, `collection.delete` removes the join rows directly, without running `GroupUser` callbacks. `GroupUser` maintains `user_count` through `belongs_to :group, counter_cache: "user_count"` (`app/models/group_user.rb:2`), and that callback never runs here. The model already has `Group#remove(user)` (`app/models/group.rb:276-278`), which destroys the `GroupUser` records and does decrement the counter. After a removal, `groups.user_count` stays at the old value, so `/admin/groups.json` and the group list keep showing the wrong count.

findings.title: Negative `offset` or `limit` on the public members endpoint reaches PostgreSQL and returns a 500
findings.description: `limit` and `offset` are parsed with `.to_i` and passed through unchecked (lines 22-23, used at line 26). `GET /groups/:name/members.json?offset=-1` produces `OFFSET -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects ("OFFSET must not be negative"), so the request fails with a 500. A negative `limit` does the same. The endpoint is public; `find_group` only checks visibility. Clamping both values to be at least 0 fixes it.

findings.title: The alias level chosen for a new group is sent by the client but ignored by `create`
findings.description: `create` sets only `name` and `visible` (lines 24-25). The client's `create()` sends `alias_level` through `asJSON()` (`models/group.js:65`, `70-75`), and the form offers the alias combo for new groups (`admin/templates/group.hbs:42-43`). The server never reads it, so every new group saves with the default alias level. The old controller also ignored it, but this diff rewrote `create` and kept the omission. `update` already handles it at line 37.

findings.title: Removing the only member on the last page leaves the admin on an empty page
findings.description: `findMembers` clamps `offset` to `user_count` (line 23), but `removeMember` calls `findMembers()` (line 47) while `user_count` still holds the pre-removal value. With 51 members on page 2 (offset 50), removing the only member on that page leaves the offset at 50 because the clamp uses the stale 51. The server answers with `members: []` and `total: 50`, so the admin sees an empty page at "2/2". Re-clamping the offset to the new total after the reload, and stepping back a page when it is past the end, fixes it.
